claims.statement: The pinned fragment describes image/PDF attachments as available on all Copilot plans and enabled by default without a policy requirement for turning the feature on or off. This does not establish present availability, permissible upload of private material, data handling guarantees, or a verified tenant setting.

The four illustrative image prompts concern explaining screenshot code, producing code from an interface mockup, describing a flowchart, and generating similar HTML from a webpage screenshot. They are suggested use cases, not file-format specifications, measured accuracy, or permission to reproduce copyrighted interfaces or upload sensitive images.

The fragment recommends scaling a previously selected solution with assigned rollout ownership, transparent goals, training, and outcome measurement. Its developer scenarios/resources are intended to support communication and training plans aligned to goals. This advisory recommendation is not an approved rollout, delivered training, assigned accountable owner, or outcome receipt.

The fragment gives a sidebar navigation path from the Copilot section to Internet access. It specifies no selected setting, firewall semantics, allowed domain list, permission requirement, or actual network behavior; navigation is not enforcement.

The Java fence contains only the beginning of a private integer-returning method with a first Date parameter followed by a comma. It is incomplete in isolation, not executable validated code or a date-calculation implementation; no correctness or compile receipt is implied.

The JetBrains fragment describes opening Copilot from the lower-right icon, opening Chat in Agent mode, selecting the MCP configuration tools icon, and choosing Add MCP Tools. It provides entry steps only, not a server configuration, credential flow, organizational authorization, or successful connection; no tools were installed.
